List What Effect
infra What a stack runs as infrastructure on a user’s cluster: alpine (the distributor), ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy (the token proxy, tag edge; until the first publication the scan reports that it cannot pull it), coredns/coredns, registry.k8s.io/pause A CRITICAL finding with a fix fails the job, and so does an infra image that Trivy cannot scan
report Job images that users choose (cimg/*) and images that only CI or a test uses HIGH and CRITICAL findings are listed and never fail the run: most carry some in any given week, from upstream packages that this repository cannot patch
skip The Windows images Listed, not scanned: Trivy finds no operating system in a Windows image when it runs on Linux and returns an empty, clean report, so the scan would claim a result it does not have

To add an image, add a line to ci/security-scan-images.txt. An image on no list fails the scan, and lint-circleci runs ci/security-scan.sh lists and fails the pull request that adds it.

What to do about a failure. The log ends with the answer: bump the digest (a Renovate pull request does it, Pinned versions), or add a justified .trivyignore entry (the CVE, the reason, an owner and an expiry date: the policy is in that file). An entry also applies to the trivy command of linux-image-example, which reads the same file but is a different check: it gates the image this repository builds, against its base.

Create the schedule

The workflow runs when the pipeline parameter security-scan is true. Nothing in the repository creates the schedule: a maintainer does this once. Use the branch main, so the scan reads the pins of main. The schedule runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC, after Renovate has opened its pull requests.

In the web app, open Project Settings, Project Setup (or Triggers), select Schedule + next to the pipeline, and set: name weekly-security-scan, branch main, pipeline attribution “The scheduling system”, parameter security-scan = true, repeats weekly on Monday, start time 06 (UTC), 1 time per hour. Enable the trigger and save.

The CircleCI CLI has no command for schedules. With the API, create a personal API token, keep it in CIRCLECI_TOKEN (never in a repository file, never printed), and run:

curl --request POST "https://circleci.com/api/v2/project/gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/schedule" \
 --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" \
 --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
 --data '{
 "name": "weekly-security-scan",
 "description": "Trivy on every pinned image and govulncheck on the proxy (docs/ci.md, Security scan)",
 "attribution-actor": "system",
 "parameters": {"branch": "main", "security-scan": true},
 "timetable": {"per-hour": 1, "hours-of-day": [6], "days-of-week": ["MON"]}
 }'

Deploys

The pipeline records its deployments in the Deploys view of CircleCI, with deploy markers: circleci run release plan creates the deploy as pending, and circleci run release update moves it to RUNNING and then to SUCCESS or FAILED. CircleCI creates the components and environments on the first deploy. ci/deploy-marker.sh makes the calls, and ci/tests/deploy-marker.sh tests it in lint-circleci against a stub of the circleci command.

Deploy Job Component Environment Version
A GitHub release release machine-runner-swarm github-releases The release tag, for example v0.2.0
The docs site docs-site-publish docs-site github-pages The commit SHA
The token proxy image of a commit proxy-image-publish token-proxy-image docker-hub sha-<12 characters of the commit>
The release tags of the image release token-proxy-image docker-hub The release number, X.Y.Z
  • Only a real deploy is recorded. The release job plans its deploy after it has the version, and only when it will publish (GITHUB_TOKEN is set). Nothing to release and a run without the token record nothing. The docs job records a deploy only with GITHUB_TOKEN, and the image jobs only with the Docker Hub credentials.
  • Failure. The release script gives the deploy FAILED, with the exit status as the reason, on every way out of the script. A failed or canceled deploy gives the live version back to the last successful one. The docs job does the same in a step with when: on_fail.
  • Cancel. A cancel that reaches ci/release.sh as a signal records CANCELED. The long step of docs-site-publish and proxy-image-publish runs under ci/deploy-marker.sh guard NAME COMMAND, which stops the command on SIGTERM or SIGINT, gives the deploy CANCELED and exits 143. A canceled step runs no later step (not even when: on_fail), so without the guard the deploy would stay RUNNING. Only a real cancel shows whether CircleCI sends the signal to the step.
  • The plan comes after the build. docs-site-publish builds first and plans afterwards, so a site that does not build is a failed job, not a FAILED deploy.
  • One job. Plan and updates are steps of one job. A rerun from failed that starts a new job would break the link between them, and CircleCI refuses a second final status for a deploy.
  • A marker never fails a job. If the task agent refuses a call (for example the organization has no Deploys), the script prints a warning and exits 0.

Pinned versions

Every tool image is pinned by tag and digest, and every download by version and SHA-256. Renovate, the GitHub App of the organization, keeps them current. renovate.json is its whole configuration: the repository needs no workflow or token for it.

  • When. Renovate opens pull requests on Monday before 06:00 UTC, at most six at a time. A major version waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
  • Commit types. A pull request that changes what users run (stack images, proxy image bases, Go toolchain for the proxy image, Windows distributor tools) is a fix(deps) commit, so the release job makes a release for it. proxy image bases are the distroless base of proxy/Dockerfile and the Nano Server digests of ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1: as ci(deps), which cliff.toml skips, the published image would keep stale base layers until an unrelated feat or fix lands. The CI-only groups are ci(deps) and the theme is docs(deps): they make no release (Releasing).
  • Digests. Renovate pins every image that carries a digest, refreshes the digest of a tag, and moves the tag and digest together. cimg/base and the e2e sweeper image circleci/runner-agent get a new digest but never a new tag: a person changes the tag.
Pin Where How Renovate finds it
Images with a digest .circleci/*.yml, linux/stack/*.yaml, windows/stack/*.yaml, ci/, the tests, the docs One regex manager for name:tag@sha256:... in any file
Hugo, lychee, the CircleCI CLI docs-site command and lint-circleci in continue.yml A # renovate: comment above the version variable
git-cliff, cosign, crane, gh, Go, govulncheck ci/release.sh, ci/tools.sh (cosign, crane), ci/security-scan.sh The same comment
Kata Containers KATA_VERSION in linux/tests/microvm.sh A regex (GitHub releases)
PortableGit, 7-Zip ReleaseTag and SevenZipVersion in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1 A regex each (GitHub releases)

To pin a new tool, put its version in one variable and add the comment # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=<owner>/<repo> extractVersion=^v(?<version>.*)$ on the line above it. The comment is the whole configuration. The versions in use are in the files of the table: continue.yml names every CI image and tool.

A pull request that needs a checksum

Renovate cannot compute a SHA-256. For a tool pinned with one (Hugo, lychee, the CircleCI CLI, git-cliff, cosign, gh, Go, Kata, PortableGit, 7-Zip, Node.js), the pull request changes the version only, carries the label checksum and a note, and its CI fails on the checksum. To finish it:

  1. Take the new value from the checksums file of the release (the table in Pinned tools names the file), or download the asset and run sha256sum on it.
  2. Replace the old value next to the version, in the same branch, and push.
  3. For PortableGit, also set Version (X.Y.Z.N for the tag vX.Y.Z.windows.N) and run ci/config-names.sh --write: the distributor is a Swarm config.
  4. Update the version in the prose that names it (Releasing, docs/microvm.md for Kata).

Pins that stay by hand

Renovate does not touch these. Change the version and its checksum together, and run the check of the job that uses it.

  • Images without a digest in the stack files (coredns/coredns, alpine:3.24 of the token proxy, the cimg classes) and the Windows servercore tags: the tag is a choice for users, and Windows tags must match the host. The weekly security scan still scans them (not the Windows images).
  • The Linux and Windows machine images (executors in continue.yml): ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1, windows-server-2022-gui:2026.05.1, windows-server-2025-gui:2026.05.1. They use dated tags, not current, which CircleCI moves every three months: an image that changes under an unrelated pull request would turn it red. Every quarter, read the image changelog, move those three tags together, and start a pipeline for the branch with full: true.
  • The Android machine image for linux-microvm: android:current. CircleCI publishes quarterly tags plus current (gen2) and default (gen1), not dated tags. Bump it by hand when the image changelog says to.
  • PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester (lint-powershell, windows-swarm, windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1).
  • The Mermaid script of the site (params.mermaid.base in site/hugo.yaml): it must match the version that the lint-docs-mermaid image bundles.
  • The runner build of the e2e sweeper: the image tag in ci/e2e-host.sh and the circleci-runner.exe URL and SHA-256 in ci/E2E-Host.ps1 move together.

To bump one by hand, resolve the new digest, update the tag and digest together, and validate the config:

docker buildx imagetools inspect <IMAGE>:<TAG>
circleci config validate .circleci/continue.yml

Cost and duration

Measured on 2026-10-13 (pipeline 9aed4106, a full run on smr-swarm/ci). Credits use the published per-minute rates (Windows medium 40, Linux xlarge 40, Linux medium and Arm medium 10, Docker small 5, Docker medium 10). The e2e probes run on self-hosted classes and cost no compute credits.

Pipeline Credits (about) Wall clock
Feature branch that changes a file every suite reads (measured with both Windows jobs) 1,500, of which the two Windows jobs are 1,200 18 min
main (every job except release) 3,800 25 min
A documentation-only pull request 200
The weekly security scan 150 a run

The measurements predate the gating: a feature branch now costs about 700 credits less (no Server 2025 job) and about 500 less when no Windows file changes (an estimate). Windows dominates the cost: every Windows job pulls the 2 GB Server Core image onto a fresh VM (about 5 to 10 minutes, in a step with no_output_timeout: 30m), and windows-swarm-ltsc2022 takes 12 min 31 s and windows-swarm-ltsc2025 about 17 min. Splitting linux-swarm bills about 1,200 credits instead of about 1,100, because three more VMs pull and set up, and the wall clock falls from about 27 minutes to about 9.

Facts about the CI machines that the design depends on

Measured on 2026-10-12. Check these first when something Swarm-related breaks in CI.

Fact Consequence
Linux machine image ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1: Docker 29.4.2 with the containerd image store (overlayfs snapshotter), on x86_64 and arm64 The writable layer is upperdir=/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/N/fs, and the probes hash it
A service with hostname: "{{.Node.Hostname}}-<service>-{{.Task.Slot}}" (the shipped Linux stack) gives every container of a slot the same hostname Probes read the full container ID from /proc/self/mountinfo (Docker bind-mounts /etc/hostname from /var/lib/docker/containers/<ID>/) and compare the writable-layer hash. The host maps the container ID to the Nth start event of the service
docker events prints an empty exitCode for start events The event format uses {{or (index .Actor.Attributes "exitCode") "-"}}, or the columns shift
Windows machine images (Server 2022 build 20348, Server 2025 build 26100): Docker 29.4.0, default isolation process Containers share the host kernel. The node must carry machine-runner-swarm.windows-<tag>=true for the stack’s placement constraint (a Server 2025 node carries both windows-ltsc2022 and windows-ltsc2025)
A Windows host runs images of its own release and older: a 2025 host also runs ltsc2022 images, a 2022 host cannot run ltsc2025 images (0xc0370101), and nested virtualisation is not available, so only process isolation works The Windows jobs pick the image tag from the host’s build number (20348: ltsc2022, 26100: ltsc2025)
docker swarm init on a Windows machine image fails with could not find the system's IP address - specify one with --advertise-addr Pass --advertise-addr with the IPv4 address of the Ethernet adapter (vEthernet (nat) has a 172.x address)
For a few seconds after docker swarm init on a Windows VM, outbound connections and DNS fail Every Windows job downloads and pulls first, and runs docker swarm init last
docker stop and docker service update end a stock Server Core container about 5 seconds after the shutdown event (HCS waits only WaitToKillServiceTimeout; exit code 3221225786, 0xC000013A), whatever it runs Every Windows service runs the stock image, and no image is built. Test-StopHandling.ps1 measures the rule (an informational NOTE control line), and the e2e never stops a busy container. The DIY image that lifts the limit is in Stop a busy Windows container and is not tested here

item.title: Releasing
item.description:
This page is for maintainers. A CircleCI job makes every release when a change is merged to main. Nobody tags a release by hand, edits a changelog, or pushes a release commit. The job creates the tag through the GitHub API.

  • Version and notes rules: cliff.toml
  • The job: release in the ci workflow of .circleci/continue.yml, and ci/release.sh
  • How users check a release: Verify a release

Make a release

  1. Bump the runner pin in a commit before the release (Bump the runner version), for example feat(runner): pin <VERSION> by default.

  2. Preview the next version and its notes in a clone with the tags:

    git cliff --bumped-version
git cliff --unreleased --tag "$(git cliff --bumped-version)" --strip header

  3. Merge the pull request to main. The pipeline runs every test, then the release job publishes.

  4. If a job fails, fix it and use Rerun workflow from failed in CircleCI.

  5. Check the release:

    gh release view <TAG> --repo CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm

    Then verify the bundle and the image, including the ref, as a user does (Verify a release).

A push with only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build commits makes no release. The job ends green with Nothing to release since vX.Y.Z.

What happens on merge

  1. The setup phase (.circleci/config.yml) passes release: true when the branch is main, both e2e tokens are present, and a commit of the push would make a release (cliff.toml). That switches on every suite, full-suite, e2e-linux, e2e-windows and strict. Otherwise it passes release: false, because a release must wait for every test.
  2. The release job requires every other job of the ci workflow except three optional ones. If one fails, nothing is released.
  3. The job runs in the serial group <project slug>/release. When a newer pipeline’s release job waits in the group, the older one skips and the newer one releases both changes.
  4. ci/release.sh checks the Swarm config names (Swarm config names) and the runner pin, computes the version and notes, pins the pipeline’s token proxy image digest in the bundle’s stack files, builds the bundles, signs SHA256SUMS and verifies the signature. It then verifies the image signature, gives the image its release tags, and creates the GitHub release, which creates the tag.
  5. When the job publishes, it records two Deploys in CircleCI: machine-runner-swarm in github-releases (version the tag), and token-proxy-image in docker-hub (version X.Y.Z). A deploy ends as SUCCESS, or FAILED when a step fails (Deploys).

A release needs the image of its commit. proxy-image-publish of the same pipeline pushes it as sha-<12 characters>, and the release requires that job. Without DOCKERHUB_USERNAME and DOCKERHUB_TOKEN in the context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub (Docker Hub context), a pipeline that is not the production main stays green and publishes nothing: the release job stores the bundle as an artifact and creates no GitHub release. On the production main the same gap fails the jobs (Publishing fails closed on main).

Other branches and tag pipelines never release. A push to main that changes only documentation has no e2e and no release job, unless a commit would make a release, such as fix(docs): (Documentation-only changes).

Add a new job to requires of the release job in .circleci/continue.yml. lint-circleci compiles the workflow and fails when a job is missing. Its $optional list is the only exception: linux-mixed-arch (the emulated mixed-architecture test), proxy-image-edge (moves the edge tag after the tests) and docs-site-comment (posts the preview address on a pull request).

Versions

The project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x. Tags are vX.Y.Z. git-cliff computes the next version from the Conventional Commits since the last tag. cliff.toml sets initial_tag = "v0.1.0" for a repository with no tag.

Commits since the last release Next version while 0.x
A breaking change: type!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer Minor, for example 0.2.3 to 0.3.0
feat Minor
fix, perf, revert Patch
Only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build No release
Not a Conventional Commit, such as a GitHub “Merge pull request” commit Ignored

A breaking change never raises the major number: 1.0.0 is a decision for people. To allow it, set breaking_always_bump_major = true and features_always_bump_minor = false in the [bump] section of cliff.toml. The next breaking change then makes 1.0.0.

Release notes

git-cliff writes the notes for the GitHub release: breaking changes first, then features, bug fixes, performance changes and reverts. The (#123) that GitHub adds to a squash merge title links to the pull request, and an entry without one links to its commit. CHANGELOG.md in the repository only points to GitHub Releases. The release bundle holds a generated CHANGELOG.md with every release.

What a release contains

Asset Content
machine-runner-swarm-<version>.tar.gz README.md, LICENSE, SECURITY.md, VERSION, the generated CHANGELOG.md, docs/, examples/, linux/ and windows/
machine-runner-swarm-<version>.zip The same files, for Windows users
SHA256SUMS The SHA-256 checksum of both bundles
SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json The cosign bundle: signature, certificate and transparency log entry

The bundles come from git archive, so only tracked files ship. They leave out linux/tests/, windows/tests/, docs/ci.md, docs/releasing.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ci/, .circleci/, proxy/ and site/. ci/bundle-links.py turns every link from a shipped page to a left-out file into a link to that file on GitHub at the release tag (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/vX.Y.Z/...), and stops the release when a link is dead in the repository too. ci/tests/bundle-links.sh tests it in lint-circleci.

The token proxy image

The token proxy is a published image, ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy on Docker Hub, not a release asset. One tag is a manifest list for linux/amd64, arm64, ppc64le and s390x, and Windows Server 2022 and 2025 (windows/amd64). There is no windows/arm64 image (install-windows.md).

Event Tags pushed
A pull request or a branch None: built and tested only
A merge to main sha-<12 characters of the commit>, by proxy-image-publish
The same merge, after the four linux-swarm jobs and every e2e group pass edge, by proxy-image-edge, the last job of the pipeline. It stays put when a newer commit is on main
A release (ci/release.sh) X.Y.Z (immutable), X.Y, X and latest, on the digest of that commit’s sha-<12> image. Nothing is rebuilt

The stack files of a checkout default to latest, so only the release job changes what a checkout deploys, and it runs after every test. edge is the newest tested commit, and sha-<12> is one commit that nothing has tested yet. Neither is a default. Before the first release, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE to a sha-<12> or edge tag, or use a release bundle.

X.Y.Z never moves: a release that finds it on another digest stops. X.Y, X and latest move only when the release is the newest of its minor line, its major line and overall. Three helper tags (sha-<12>-linux, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2022, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2025) hold parts of the manifest list: do not pull them.

The pipeline builds and runs each image (ci/proxy-image.sh, ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1, jobs in CI/CD). On main (the pipeline parameter publish), proxy-image-publish joins the helper images with crane index append, tags the list sha-<12>, checks every platform, and signs every digest keyless with the CircleCI OIDC token. The release job pins the digest in the bundle’s stack files (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE:-ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:<version>@sha256:<digest>, in place of :latest), checks the signature, and adds the four release tags.

A checkout keeps latest, which Renovate does not manage. A release bundle carries its own digest, and it is the documented way to install. Users verify the image with cosign (Verify the token proxy image) and must check that the certificate names refs/heads/main (How the signature works).

Bump the runner version

The stack files pin one exact runner version by default: MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION: ${MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION:-3.1.13} in the distributor settings of linux/stack/runners.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml, and in x-env of linux/stack/microvm.yaml. It is the newest version that CI tests (STACK_RUNNER_PIN in linux/tests/lib.sh), so a release carries the pin that CI tested. Bump it in a commit before each release:

  1. Pick the newest version in the manifest that has linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x and windows amd64, arm64. List versions with jq -r '.releases | keys[]' manifest.json and check .releases["<version>"]. Read the runner changelog.
  2. In one commit, change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION in all three stack files. Change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 to the tarball SHA-256 values of that version (from the release’s checksums.txt or the manifest), comma-separated: linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x in linux/stack/runners.yaml and linux/stack/microvm.yaml, and windows amd64, arm64 in windows/stack/runners.yaml.
  3. Commit it as feat(runner): pin 3.1.14 by default for a new minor or patch that users should get, or fix(runner): ... for a fix, so that git-cliff makes a release. Let CI run.
  4. Update the docs examples (docs/operations.md uses 3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only when you want them to move.

The version must be equal in every file: linux/tests/stack-config.sh fails when it differs. The release job (check_runner_pin in ci/release.sh) fails when the version is not in the manifest for every platform, or when a default SHA-256 list does not match the manifest. A user gets the new runner by deploying the new release. A user who sets the variable keeps what they set.

How the signature works

The job gets an OIDC token with circleci run oidc get --claims '{"aud":"sigstore"}' --root-issuer. The audience sigstore and the issuer https://oidc.circleci.com are what the public Sigstore certificate authority (Fulcio) accepts for CircleCI. cosign sign-blob swaps the token for a short-lived certificate, signs SHA256SUMS and records the signature in the public Rekor log. No key is kept.

The certificate identity is https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects/<project-id>/pipeline-definitions/<pipeline-definition-id>. It is the same for every branch, and a job of any branch can get an OIDC token with no context, so the identity alone does not prove that main signed. The source repository ref does: the certificate extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14, which Fulcio fills from the vcs-ref claim. It is refs/heads/main for a release and refs/heads/<branch> for any other branch.

cosign has flags for the GitHub extensions only, so ci/tools.sh reads the certificate itself (signed_only_on, tested by ci/tests/signature-ref.sh):

  • ci/release.sh runs cosign verify-blob on SHA256SUMS, then checks that the certificate names refs/heads/main. The job stops if it does not.
  • ci/proxy-image.sh does the same for every digest of the token proxy image, right after signing and again in the release job before the release tags. It reads every signature of the digest (cosign download signature): one signature of a feature branch next to one of main fails the check.

To check the ref by hand, after cosign verify-blob printed Verified OK, run this. The hex string is the OID followed by refs/heads/main, so it matches the whole value:

jq -r '.verificationMaterial | (.certificate // .x509CertificateChain.certificates[0]).rawBytes' SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json | base64 -d \
 | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | grep -Eq '^([0-9a-f]{2})*2b0601040183bf30010e0411(0c|13)0f726566732f68656164732f6d61696e' \
 && echo "signed for refs/heads/main" || echo "NOT signed for refs/heads/main: do not use this release"

CircleCI documents OIDC tokens for jobs that use a context. In a test on 2026-10-13, circleci run oidc get also worked in a job without one, which is why the ref and not the identity decides.

Where the signature of the image is stored, and the tries

cosign 3.1.3 stores an image signature as a Sigstore bundle, pushed as an OCI 1.1 referrer of the signed digest. cosign verify and cosign download signature fall back to the older sha256-<hex>.sig tag only when they find no referrer (the source of no signatures found). ci/proxy-image.sh pins the format with --new-bundle-format=true on both commands (the variable cosign_storage). The flag is the default of 3.1.3 and deprecated: when a cosign version drops it, the rehearsal of the pull request that updates cosign fails, and main does not.

Docker Hub probably does not list a referrer at once: the first run on main failed with no signatures found right after cosign sign. verify_signature therefore tries up to six times, waiting 5, 10, 15, 25 and 35 seconds between tries (SIGN_VERIFY_DELAYS sets the waits). Every check stays whole in every try: identity, issuer, and the ref refs/heads/main on every signature. A signature that names another ref fails at once. After the last failed try, the job prints cosign tree of the digest and the repository tags that start with sha256-.

The signing rehearsal

Signing runs for real on main only, so a failure would first show on a merge and leave sha-<12> tags with no release. The job signing-rehearsal runs the same code in every pipeline that is not documentation-only, on any branch, with no context and no secret (ci/proxy-image.sh rehearse):

  1. It pushes a throwaway image to a registry:2 container of the job at localhost:5000.
  2. It signs the image against the real Fulcio and Rekor (a brief failure is tried again, three times) and verifies it with verify_signature, the function that main uses, for the ref refs/heads/<branch of the pipeline>.
  3. It checks that the same signature is refused for another ref, so a check that stopped looking at the ref turns the pipeline red.

Each rehearsal adds an entry to the public Rekor log with the project, branch and commit. The release requires the job.

Enable publishing

Until you do this, the release job runs every step except the last and stays green on a project with no e2e tokens. It prints publishing skipped: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set in context scalable-machine-runner-release and keeps the version, notes, bundles and signature as job artifacts. On the production main (both e2e tokens present) it fails with the same message.

  1. Create a fine-grained personal access token with the resource owner CircleCI-Labs, only this repository, and the repository permission Contents: Read and write. Nothing else is needed, because gh release create makes the tag and the release. The token expires, so note the date to rotate it. A GitHub App installation token expires after one hour, so it does not fit a context variable.

  2. In the CircleCI organization settings, create the context scalable-machine-runner-release and add the variable GITHUB_TOKEN with the token.

  3. Restrict the context to this project, and add an expression restriction so that only pipelines of main can use it, not an SSH rerun that could print the token and not an API pipeline (which can name any branch and may bring its own config):

    pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")

    With the CLI, where <PROJECT_ID> is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:

    circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org <ORG> --type project --value <PROJECT_ID>
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org <ORG> --type expression \
 --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")'

    In the organization’s advanced settings, leave pipelines with an unversioned config off.

  4. In the project settings (Advanced), keep Build forked pull requests and Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests off.

  5. Protect main with the ruleset in A ruleset for main: a pull request required, no force push, no bypass, and the check ci. Whoever can change .circleci/ or ci/release.sh on main controls what runs with the token. What the release trust depends on lists every setting that the signature relies on.

The docs site, its pull request comment and the weekly security scan have their own contexts (What a maintainer creates once). Do not reuse this token for them: it can publish releases. The next release run on main publishes. To check before then, read the release job log for publishing skipped.

What the release trust depends on

A valid signature says one thing: a job of this CircleCI project, from the pipeline definition of this repository, ran on refs/heads/main of this repository. The claim holds only as far as the settings below hold. They are settings of GitHub, CircleCI and Docker Hub, not of the repository, so no file can enforce or show them, and ci/release.sh does not check them. The maintainers have set all of them for v0.1.0. Check the settings says how to read them back.

The main-only expression below is the one in Enable publishing step 3. Every context also has a project restriction (this project).

Setting Where It must say Without it
Ruleset of main GitHub repository Require a pull request. Block force pushes. Restrict deletions. No bypass list. Required status check: ci (A ruleset for main) A writer could push a change of .circleci/ or ci/release.sh to main, and it would be signed
Ruleset of smr-swarm/** GitHub repository Restrict creations and updates, maintainers alone on the bypass list (The e2e context and smr-swarm/*) A writer could print the e2e runner tokens in a public log from an smr-swarm/<name> branch
Context scalable-machine-runner-release CircleCI organization project and the main-only expression Another branch, an SSH rerun or an API pipeline could read the token
Context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub CircleCI organization The same two restrictions (The Docker Hub context) A branch could push the image that the stack files name
Context scalable-machine-runner-docs CircleCI organization The same two restrictions A branch could read a token that can write to the repository
Context scalable-machine-runner-e2e CircleCI organization project, and the main-only expression with (pipeline.git.branch == "main" or pipeline.git.branch starts-with "smr-swarm/") in place of the branch test A branch could read the e2e runner tokens
Context scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments CircleCI organization project, and the main-only expression without the branch test. Any branch pusher can read it, so its token has the least permission (Docs site previews) An SSH rerun or an API pipeline could read it
Project settings CircleCI project and organization Build forked pull requests, Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests, Auto-cancel redundant workflows, SSH reruns and pipelines with an unversioned config: all off (Secrets and public logs) A fork or an API pipeline could run a config of its own
Tokens GitHub, Docker Hub Release and docs tokens: fine-grained, this repository only, Contents: Read and write. Comment token: Issues: Read and write, of a bot account. Docker Hub token: read and write on ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy only, from an account with two-factor authentication (What each job can see) A leaked token would reach more than the job that needs it

Two things are not covered. The signature does not say that anyone reviewed the change (the ruleset sets the number of reviews, and .github/CODEOWNERS asks the same people for every path), and it says nothing about main before the ruleset existed.

Check the settings

Read the GitHub settings back with the API. The first command lists the rules that apply to main (it must include pull_request, non_fast_forward, deletion and required_status_checks). The second and third show the bypass list of a ruleset, which must be empty for main:

gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].type'
gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets --jq '.[] | "\(.id) \(.name) \(.enforcement)"'
gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets/<ID> --jq '{conditions, bypass_actors, rules: [.rules[].type]}'

The ruleset of smr-swarm/** must show creation and update. The CLI cannot list context restrictions, so read them from the API for each of the five contexts and compare them with the table. Find a context id with circleci context list --org <ORG>:

curl -s --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" https://circleci.com/api/v2/context/<CONTEXT_ID>/restrictions

The project settings are in the web app (Project Settings, then Advanced), and the Docker Hub token scope is in the account’s security settings. Keep the output with the release pull request.

Rotate the e2e runner tokens

Rotate both e2e runner tokens when one may have leaked, and when someone who could read them leaves the project. For each class, create a new token, store it in the context, run one pipeline on main and check that both e2e groups pass, then delete the old token. circleci context secret set prompts for the value in a terminal, so the token stays out of the shell history:

circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux --nickname ci-YYYYMM
circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org <ORG> --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX
circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows --nickname ci-YYYYMM
circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org <ORG> --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS
circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux
circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows
circleci runner token delete <OLD_TOKEN_ID>

Merge method

The notes come from the commits on main, so the merge method decides what they show.

  • Merge commit or rebase and merge. Every commit of the pull request gets its own entry, so use it for small, atomic Conventional Commits (Commit messages). The GitHub merge commit is not a Conventional Commit, so the notes ignore it.
  • Squash and merge. The pull request becomes one commit with its title as the message, and one entry that links to the pull request. Write the title as a Conventional Commit. A pull request that mixes a feat and a fix loses one of them.

Mark a breaking change with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer, in a commit message or in the title of a squashed pull request.

Tag pipelines

The project uses the GitHub OAuth integration (project slug gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm), which has no trigger settings: CircleCI starts a pipeline for every push that GitHub reports, so the tag that the release creates starts one. In it, pipeline.git.tag is the tag, and pipeline.git.branch and CIRCLE_BRANCH are empty.

That pipeline cannot release and runs no job. CircleCI runs no job for a tag unless the job has a tag filter, and no job in .circleci/ has one. To build for tags, give a job a tag filter on purpose, and keep the release context out of that job.

Rerun and recovery

Rerunning is safe. Before it publishes, the job looks for a release tag at its commit, and it never creates a second release. Rerunning a pipeline from before a later release releases nothing.

Situation What to do
The release job failed before it published Rerun the job. It computes the same version
An asset of an existing release is missing Rerun the job. It uploads all assets again with --clobber
A tag exists at another commit Stop. Somebody created vX.Y.Z by hand, or an older release was moved. Compare git rev-parse vX.Y.Z with the commit of the pipeline. Delete the wrong tag and release with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag, then rerun the job
This commit is already part of vX.Y.Z A later commit was already released. The job did nothing
The release job shows as skipped A newer pipeline waits for the release lock and will release this change too
The Deploys view shows FAILED Read the reason there, fix the cause and rerun the job. It records a new deploy of the same version
gh fails with 401 or 403 The token expired or lost its permission. Replace GITHUB_TOKEN in the context and rerun the job
A release is wrong Prefer a new release that fixes it. If you delete a release and its tag, the next run makes the same version again

Pinned tools

ci/release.sh install-tools installs the tools of the job. Each download is checked against a SHA-256 value in the script (cosign and crane are in ci/tools.sh), and the job image is pinned by digest. Each tool has its version and SHA-256 value in two variables, with a # renovate: comment above the version.

Tool Version Source of the SHA-256 value
git-cliff 2.14.2 The .sha512 file of the release, and a local sha256sum
cosign 3.1.3 cosign_checksums.txt of the release
crane 0.22.1 checksums.txt of the release (the Linux x86_64 archive)
gh 2.102.0 gh_2.102.0_checksums.txt of the release
Go 1.27.2 The download page of go.dev, next to the archive
cimg/base 2026.10 The digest in .circleci/continue.yml

Renovate opens a pull request that changes the version only. It has the label checksum and fails on the checksum until you replace the SHA-256 value in the same branch. To update a tool by hand, change its version and SHA-256 value together in install_tools (cosign and crane: in ci/tools.sh), then follow Try it locally. To update the job image, follow Pinned versions. A Renovate pull request for Go also moves the golang and cimg/go images, so the release proxy binaries use the same Go as proxy-test.

Try it locally

Everything except publishing and signing runs on an x86_64 Linux workstation. The first command installs git-cliff, cosign, crane and gh into ~/.local/bin, and Go into ~/.local/go. The second writes the files to /tmp/release and signs and publishes nothing.

ci/release.sh install-tools
RELEASE_SKIP_SIGN=1 ci/release.sh

To check that the release job requires every job of the workflow, as lint-circleci does, compile the config with every parameter on and read the release entry of workflows.ci.jobs:

circleci config process .circleci/continue.yml \
 --pipeline-parameters '{full-suite: true, e2e-linux: true, e2e-windows: true, release: true, publish: true}'

Move the project to CircleCI-Public

Replace the Labs wording in the banner and the Support section of README.md, SECURITY.md, the support paragraph at the top of CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, and .github/CODEOWNERS. Decide the license, because CircleCI runner repositories use Apache-2.0 and this one uses MIT.

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Thank you for helping to improve machine runner swarm, a CircleCI Labs project. Field engineers review issues and pull requests on a best-effort basis, with no SLA. Report a security problem by email, not in an issue (SECURITY.md).

Reporting a bug

Search the existing issues first, and check that you use the latest release. Then open a new issue with the bug template. Include:

  • The release or commit, and the runner version. On Linux, run docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION on the node. On Windows, run docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows.
  • The operating system of the node and the Docker Engine version.
  • The output of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<SERVICE> and docker service logs --tail 100 runners_<SERVICE>.

Remove tokens, runner config files, and internal host names from everything you paste.

Requesting a feature

Open an issue with the feature request template. Describe the problem, and name the platform and the files it affects. For problems in the CircleCI platform or the runner agent, contact CircleCI support instead.

Opening a pull request

Before you open a pull request:

  1. Discuss large changes in an issue first.
  2. Run the tests for the platform you changed (Development).
  3. Update docs/ when you change a variable, label, secret, port, or default.
  4. Write every commit message, and the pull request title, as a Conventional Commit (Commit messages). The release notes are generated from them, so there is no changelog entry to add.
  5. Check that the diff has no tokens, host names, or customer or vendor names. The repository is public.

A pull request from a fork gets no CI. The project builds no forked pull request and passes no secret to one (Secrets and public logs). A maintainer reads the change and, to run CI, pushes its commits to a branch of the project by hand. Never push or mirror an outside branch to main or to a branch named smr-swarm/*: those names get the e2e runner tokens and, on main, the publishing contexts, and a job takes its configuration from its own branch.

A pull request that changes only documentation (docs/, site/, Markdown files) runs the lint jobs and the docs site build, and skips the builds and the Swarm tests (Documentation-only changes).

Use the pull request template. Maintainers choose the merge method: a squash merge turns the pull request title into the commit message on main, and a merge commit or rebase keeps your commits (Merge method).

Commit messages

Use Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary. The release job reads these messages to choose the version and write the release notes. Keep each commit small and atomic.

Type Use for
feat A new capability, or a changed stack-file contract
fix A bug fix
docs Documentation only
test Tests only
ci The CircleCI pipeline
chore Maintenance with no user-visible change
refactor, perf Code changes that keep behavior, or improve speed

Common scopes are linux, windows, docs, readme, and ci.

A breaking change appears first in the release notes, and while the version is 0.x it raises the minor number. Mark it in one of two ways, and write what the user has to change:

  • Add ! after the type or scope: feat(linux)!: rename the persistent service.

  • Add a BREAKING CHANGE: footer:

    feat(linux): rename the persistent service

BREAKING CHANGE: the service is now linux-persistent. Rename it in your stack file.

Development

Requirements: Docker with privileged containers for the Linux suite, bash, and PowerShell 7 for the Windows unit tests.

linux/tests/run-all.sh
linux/tests/run-all.sh token drain
linux/tests/stack-config.sh
pwsh -File windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 -InstallModules

The commands run the whole Linux suite, a subset, the stack file contract (no daemon needed), and the Windows unit tests (PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester).

The Linux tests run a Swarm inside docker:dind containers, so your own Docker engine never enters Swarm mode. Each test prints RESULT lines and exits 0 when it passes. CI runs the Windows Swarm tests on Windows Server 2022 and 2025. CI/CD lists the pipeline and every lint command.

CI runs the Linux groups as four parallel jobs, each with its own list (linux-swarm in .circleci/continue.yml). Add a new test to all in run-all.sh and to one of those lists: lint-circleci fails when a group is in no list or in two (Linux jobs without a token).

Test What it checks
stack-config.sh docker stack config for every combination of stack files, and the Swarm config names
helper.sh setup.sh --swarm-init, --secret and --deploy on a fresh Docker-in-Docker daemon
ephemerality.sh A new container for every job and no residue, with docker run --restart always as the negative control
exit80.sh The restart delay, no hot loop, and the exit codes 80 and 1 of the real runner
token.sh What a job can read in the default class and in the hardened class
task.sh The real runner runs tasks as the job user, also with CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR=true and as a persistent runner
proxy.sh The token proxy image in a Swarm, in front of the real runner
placement.sh Placement on a manager and a worker, and docker-build.yaml
distributor.sh The runner-distributor service: install, upgrade, rollback, pins, floating versions, pruning, a tampered binary, a wrong SHA-256, and CircleCI’s real manifest. Needs network access
persistent.sh Continuous mode and persistent.yaml
microvm.sh The microVM add-on with Kata Containers. Skipped without /dev/kvm. Downloads Kata (about 1 GB) unless SWARM_TEST_KATA_DIR or SWARM_TEST_KATA_TARBALL points at a copy. Not part of run-all.sh
drain.sh SIGTERM during a job: the job finishes
limits.sh init, ulimits, pids, memory, CPU, reservations, and the capability sets
network.sh Network isolation between classes, and between the replicas of a class
container-mode.sh The prototype container agent in a Swarm, against a fake API. Needs the Go and pause images
bats/run.sh The entrypoint unit tests on cimg/base, Alpine, and UBI minimal

The suite needs no installed runner: the distributor of the shipped stack installs one from a small HTTP mirror in the harness. Most tests publish fake-runner.sh, and task.sh, token.sh, exit80.sh, placement.sh, distributor.sh and the idle case of drain.sh publish the real runner binary, which the harness downloads once and checks against the SHA-256 of CircleCI’s manifest.

Three variables change the setup: SWARM_TEST_DIND_IMAGE sets the Docker-in-Docker image, SWARM_TEST_CACHE sets the directory that caches the real runner binary (~/.cache/swarm-tests by default), and SWARM_TEST_KEEP=1 keeps the containers for debugging.

The Windows tests in windows/tests print CHECK <NAME> PASS|FAIL lines and one RESULT line, and exit 0 only when every check passes. Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 runs the Pester tests on any system with PowerShell 7. The Test-*.ps1 scripts (Injection, Ephemerality, Exit80, Placement, StopHandling, Install, Distributor and Persistent) need a Windows host with Docker in Windows-container mode and no runner token. Each script’s header says what it checks. Test-Injection.ps1 -Online and Test-StopHandling.ps1 -Online use the real runner.

Swarm config names

The entrypoint and distributor scripts reach the nodes as Swarm configs. A Swarm config cannot change, and a service keeps the old file when the name stays, so the name of each config in the stack files carries the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its file. After you change linux/stack/circleci-runner-entrypoint, linux/stack/runner-distributor.sh, windows/runner-distributor.ps1, or a file of linux/stack/container-agent, run ci/config-names.sh --write and commit the new names with the change. lint-stack, linux/tests/stack-config.sh and the release job fail on a stale name.

Documentation checks

Documentation follows the CircleCI docs style: sentence-case headings, active voice, no contractions, and short sentences. Every docs/*.md page has front matter with page-title, page-audience, and page-description. CI checks the relative links and the Mermaid diagrams. To run the same checks locally:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/input" -w /input lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2 --config lychee.toml './**/*.md'
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/workdir" davidanson/markdownlint-cli2:v0.18.1 '**/*.md'

Pinned versions and releases

Renovate opens a pull request every Monday for the pinned versions: images and digests, the tools that CI downloads, the Go toolchain and the docs theme (renovate.json; Pinned versions lists what it covers). A pull request with the label checksum changes a version that is pinned with a SHA-256 value. Renovate cannot compute the value, so replace it in the same branch before you merge.

Pin images by tag and digest, and a new download by its version and checksum together, with a # renovate: comment above the version. The default runner version is pinned in three files that must stay equal (linux/stack/runners.yaml, linux/stack/microvm.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml), and each release bumps it (how). The pinned Git and 7-Zip versions and their SHA-256 values are in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1, and a change of the script needs ci/config-names.sh --write.

Nobody tags a release or edits a changelog: a CircleCI job on main reads the Conventional Commits, and a push with only docs, test, ci, chore, style, or refactor commits makes no release (Releasing, CHANGELOG.md).
